specification.title: A nested scope fails; the caller handles the failure and commits
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `outer` through the framework's ordinary write API. The framework decides when it is sent: one with a unit of work may keep it pending.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure that write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() (the top-level transaction's ID) and pg_backend_pid().
Raise an application error in the nested scope.
The outer scope catches the error and ends normally.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When a nested scope (a savepoint) fails, and the caller handles the failure and commits, PostgreSQL commits all of the caller's writes and none of the nested scope's writes.

execution.description: Positive control. BeginTransactionAsync, parameterized commands, CommitAsync or RollbackAsync. CommitAsync is reported as committed only when a prior SELECT 1 succeeded. A 25P02 from that probe, followed by CommitAsync returning, is reported as rolled_back. The command tag is not read. A thrown CommitAsync is reported as failed and the connection is disposed. A failed RollbackAsync(savepoint) is followed by RollbackAsync, not CommitAsync. A thrown RollbackAsync disposes the connection. IsolationLevel is passed to BeginTransactionAsync. Pooling is off.

configuration.commit_outcome: CommitAsync after SELECT 1; rolled_back when the probe failed with 25P02; the command tag is not read

execution.form: The outer transaction is BeginTransactionAsync. The nested scope is SaveAsync, RollbackAsync(name), and ReleaseAsync on that NpgsqlTransaction. There is no second connection.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: The caller knows that the nested scope failed: its error reached the caller. PostgreSQL answers the final COMMIT with COMMIT.

api_outcome.basis: SELECT 1 succeeded before CommitAsync, so the session was not in a failed transaction block, and CommitAsync returned. The command tag is not exposed. The policy does not treat a bare return, with no prior probe, as a commit.
api_outcome.contract: The correct npgsql-control policy uses NpgsqlConnection.BeginTransactionAsync, NpgsqlTransaction.CommitAsync, RollbackAsync, SaveAsync, RollbackAsync(name), and ReleaseAsync. Npgsql 10.0.3 CommitAsync sends COMMIT and waits for CommandComplete and ReadyForQuery. ExecuteInternalCommand does not read the command tag. TransactionStatus on the connector is internal and is Idle after both a committed transaction and a COMMIT that PostgreSQL answered with ROLLBACK. The public transaction API does not expose either fact. Before CommitAsync the policy runs SELECT 1 on the same connection. SQLSTATE 25P02 means the session is in a failed transaction block. If that probe fails with 25P02 and CommitAsync returns, the policy reports rolled_back and says it did not read the tag. If the probe succeeds and CommitAsync returns, the policy reports committed. A return from CommitAsync with no probe is not reported as a commit. If CommitAsync throws, the policy reports failed and disposes the connection. If RollbackAsync throws, it disposes the connection and does not call CommitAsync. A failed RollbackAsync(savepoint) is followed by RollbackAsync of the surrounding transaction. IsolationLevel is passed to BeginTransactionAsync.
